newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary minister resigns over health care spending.
newsitem.headline: Hungary minister resigns over health care spending.

text.p: Hungarian Welfare Minister Gyorgy Szabo said on Tuesday he had resigned because he was dissatisfied with the amount of public funding for health care.
"Hungarian health care is in a really difficult situation," Szabo, whose resignation had been accepted by Prime Minister Gyula Horn on Monday, told a news conference.
Hungarian health care is funded by payments from employers and workers, with the government making up for any deficit in the system.
Szabo said some health care spending could be cut by targeting inefficiency, but said he had sparred with the Finance Ministry over what he called needed investments for the coming years.
"I suppose this would lead to the same problems we had this year. Debt grows, hospitals run out of funds for drugs and there are problems in ambulance services," Szabo told Reuters.
"People cannot bear that the system cannot take care of them when they are the most helpless."
Szabo's successor has not been named.
